props.title: Markets, libraries, rec centers, and the summer series.

rows.text: A singer with a guitar, a solo guitarist or an acoustic duo, playing a market morning in sets, on a battery-powered system or none at all where the market has no power. The musician plays the folk, country and singer-songwriter songs people know the words to, at a volume the stall next door can still sell over, and a whole season of Saturdays can be booked with one enquiry.

An adult program in the meeting space, a concert series on the lawn in summer, an older adults’ afternoon with the standards, a Sunday jazz duo in the atrium, or a sound bath for a wellness program with the lights down. A library is built for quiet, so the sizes are solo and duo, and a guitarist plays a meeting space without amplification at all. René Moffatt is a featured artist of the Denver Public Library’s own Volume Denver program, and Your Bird Can Sing plays the Beatles for an all-ages afternoon, the songbook a hall of strangers between six and ninety already shares.

A community evening, a holiday open house, a summer concert in the park behind the building, an older adults’ lunch with a guitarist, a family day with a singer. The Americana band plays the outdoor evening at trio or quartet size, and a solo or a duo plays everything indoors.

A city’s or a district’s summer series is booked months ahead, often through a call for performers. The acts that play a park stage with a real sound system are the Americana band, Tejas Singh, Tony Medina, René Moffatt with his band, and the yacht rock band. Send the call and we’ll answer it with the act that fits the stage.

items.q: Do you book musicians for farmers markets?
items.a: Yes, for a morning or a whole season of Saturdays in one enquiry. Tell us the market, the hours and whether there's power, and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price. Signet Artists books community performers across Denver and the Front Range.

At a market, loud enough to hear from the next stall and quiet enough that the stall can still sell. In a library, about the level of a conversation, and a guitarist in a meeting space plays with no amplification at all. On a park stage, a band plays like a band, within whatever the permit allows.

Not much for a guitarist or a singer with a guitar, who play on a battery-powered system or without one. A band with drums needs one dedicated 20-amp circuit, and a park stage with its own sound system needs a word with whoever runs it beforehand. Every size needs a covered, level and dry spot and a rain call written down before the day. A park or a plaza sometimes needs a permit for amplified sound, usually held by the market or the city; where the answer is no amplification, the acoustic sizes play without it.

items.q: How much space does it need?
items.a: About 6 by 4 feet for a solo, 8 by 6 for a duo and 12 by 8 for a trio, on the ground or on a stage. Setup takes 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo or a trio, before the program starts.

items.q: Do you work with purchase orders and city vendor paperwork?
items.a: Yes. A W-9, a certificate of insurance naming the city, the district or the library as additional insured, and one itemized invoice that matches the purchase order come in the same email as the contract, so a business office can set up the vendor before the first date.
